_comment: Ships trade: they buy a commodity at one port and sell it at the next (see data/markets.json, where ships also buy their own fuel at a price that follows the local oil price). starting_money covers a first ship and its first cargo. Breakdowns (from company level min_company_level): every interval_s seconds, each ship at sea (not recovery boats) rolls its own chance of losing hit of its maintenance (0.5 = 50 points). The chance runs from chance_at_full at 100% maintenance to chance_at_empty at 0%, times the model's breakdown_factor (bigger ships are sturdier), times an age factor (1 + age_per_hour_at_sea for each hour the ship has spent at sea, up to max_age_factor), less the durability skill. initial_view_width_deg: how many degrees of the globe the map shows across when it opens, centered on the home port.
_company_colors_comment: Colors a new company can choose (its name in the top bar and the rings around its HQ and hubs): [id, name, hex], in picker order.
_seasons_comment: Seasonal closures (scripts/sim/seasons.gd), for saves founded with them, from company level min_company_level. Each closure shuts a canal's locks (canal), some ports (ports) or a stretch of sea (circles: [lon, lat, radius nm]; every lane through it) from from to to ([month, day], wrapping past the new year when from is later), on its real dates; not_first_year spares the game's first calendar year; ice is the circles of frozen water drawn on the map (else its circles or its icebreaker area's). A ship won't start a leg it can't finish before one shuts: it waits in port (not a hold: nothing for the player to do) until it reopens; ships already at sea finish. label names a stretch of sea on the map all year (at the middle of its circles). ice ([lon, lat, radius nm] circles) is where a port closure's sea ice is drawn on the map (closures over a stretch of sea, and those an icebreaker area covers, draw their own circles). Ice zones stay open, but ships within radius_nm of center (lon, lat) crawl at speed and wear faster (wear) in their season, fuel per mile the same. The activity log warns warn_days calendar days before a closure that touches the player's ports or routes, and when it shuts and reopens.
_icebreaking_comment: Icebreakers (scripts/sim/icebreaking.gd). Each ice area is covered by circles ([lon, lat, radius nm]) and is in season while its seasonal closure (closure) or ice zone (zone) is. With an icebreaker stationed there (station_ports: where it waits), the closure is lifted for ships it can lead (the Great Lakes locks still shut regardless): ships reaching the ice edge, or leaving a port in the ice, wait (engines off) for the icebreaker, which leads up to convoy_size ships on the same lane through the ice at escort_speed (by icebreaker kind: a share of the slower of it and the slowest ship), gap_nm apart (wide enough that each ship shows on its own at the opening zoom), then goes back for the next. An ice zone that stays open anyway (the Gulf of Finland) has no convoys: an icebreaker stationed there keeps the fairways open, so ships in it sail at fairway speed and wear instead of crawling. Icebreakers pay their own fuel and repairs.
_docks_comment: Berths (scripts/sim/docks.gd; the marina each port is drawn as, scripts/ui/map_view.gd): each port size band's berths in order round its marina (the +y side from the entrance in, then the -y side: the first each side along the first pier's seaward face, open to the outer harbour, then one between each pier and the next, the last along the land end), one letter each: L a long pier that takes any ship the port takes (the rule now: every pier is as long as the longest ship the port takes), s a berth only for the smaller ships (those that can dock at a Small port), m one for any ship a Medium port takes, B an old big berth only the biggest ships use. hub_berths: any port with an HQ or hub, so any HQ or hub can take the biggest ships. Cargo ships queue at the anchorage for a berth, first come first served, come in through the entrance and down the channel, round into their slot and alongside, and pull out backwards, at their own speed (slowing only to come alongside, sliding the last slide_s on their thrusters; in_s and out_s when there's no map to measure the way); a ship with nothing to do comes in to a pier while the port has berths to spare, else lies at the anchorage; tugs moor along the inside of the jetty's arms, other service ships lie at the anchorage.
_weather_comment: Storms (scripts/sim/weather.gd), for saves founded with Moderate or Harsh storms. From company level min_company_level they slow ships, wear them and make breakdowns likelier, and the strongest hurricane, typhoon and cyclone cores close ports; before that (and in saves without storms) nothing happens to ships, though storms are still drawn. levels: slow is the most a storm's core cuts speed (fuel per mile stays the same, so a storm alone can't strand a ship), wear the most it multiplies wear and breakdown chance, close_at how strong a tropical storm must be over a port to close it (0..1), rate how many storms form, times the basins' per_year. Each basin forms storms of its kind in its months (1-12; peak months twice as often), per_year a year on average, somewhere in spawn ([[lon min, lon max], [lat min, lat max]]), with a radius_nm of effect, lasting life_days (a calendar day is 72 s of play), moving speed_nm calendar nm an hour (about knots). Tropical kinds (hurricane, typhoon, cyclone) drift west and poleward, then curve away east past recurve_lat; gales run east. names are used in turn.
_calendar_comment: The in-game calendar starts at start (UTC) and runs minutes_per_second calendar minutes per second of play at 1x, matched to real ship speeds: a Scooter's 5.44 nm a second is about 16 knots, so Rome to Tunis takes about 20 hours on the calendar and Shanghai to Rotterdam about a month.
_rough_seas_comment: Rough seas far south: ships wear wear_factor times as fast south of lat, and cargo on legs to or from a port south of it sells for pay_bonus more. upper_lakes_bonus: cargo on legs between two ports on the upper Great Lakes (Superior, Michigan, Huron: ports.json lake) sells for that much more, like the real ore and grain trade.
_currents_comment: Ocean currents (data/currents.json, Currents). A ship sails faster with a current and slower against it, by (ref_speed_kn + the current along its way) / ref_speed_kn, at most limit either way (fuel burns by the second, so it follows the time). The lane tool (--currents-only) plans a second way round for a lane, one way, riding a current, where it beats the lane by at least min_gain of the time in some months and is at most max_detour times as long; a ship takes it in those months. ride_min_nm: the least a second way rides a current; cut_nm: how far from each port it leaves and rejoins the lane (beyond the approach channels).
_harbor_speed_comment: Ships easing out of port and into the next at sea: leaving, a ship would build up from start x its speed to full speed over about seconds of sailing (steady acceleration), and arriving slow the same way, in steps pieces each (the zones fuel, range and arrival times are worked out over, like the convoy canals); on a leg too short for both, each takes half of it. start 1.0: off, ships keep their speed right up to the harbour mouth and away from it (they get going and slow down inside their marina instead: scripts/ui/map_view.gd _sailed_share()).
_port_fee_comment: A share of each trade's margin (what the cargo sold for, less what it cost; nothing on a loss) paid as a port fee where a cargo is sold, at every port the company has no HQ or hub at.
_crew_comment: Crew wages (scripts/autoload/game_state.gd _pay_wages()): every ship has captains and crew by its tier (ship_models.json tier 1-5: captains[tier - 1] and crew[tier - 1]), paid every period_days calendar days (two weeks, about 17 minutes of play): captain_wage a captain and crew_wage a crew member, for every ship that worked in that time (sailing, or doing a stop in port); ships idle the whole time pay nothing. Set so wages are about 20% of a Scooter's profit and 5% of a Dominator's on an average route. They may take the company's money below $0: a company in debt runs its ships on credit but can't buy anything until it's back above $0.
_loans_comment: Loans (scripts/autoload/game_state.gd take_loan()): on the Finances screen a company can borrow step at a time up to max, and pay it back a step at a time; yearly_interest is charged on what it owes, a period's share each crew payday.
_xp_comment: XP: every delivery (when unloading finishes) gives the company and the ship XP for the work done: units x leg distance x xp_per_container_nm, weighted by the commodity's base price against markets.json xp_ref_price (whatever it sold for). Company levels run 1 to max_company_level. Level L costs (company_level_minutes[0] + company_level_minutes[1] x (L - 1)) minutes of the XP a full fleet at that level would earn at sea (at_sea_share of the time): every unlocked cargo model with all the slots it has at that level. So each level takes about as long no matter how big the fleet has become, and level 100 takes about 20 hours. ship_slots: how many of each model you can own. [start, every]: a model gets start slots when it unlocks and one more every that many company levels (or every slot_every levels, if the model sets it in ship_models.json), up to its max_owned. cargo is container ships and gas tankers, recovery is recovery boats. Ships level 0 to ship_max_level, one skill point per level; see ship_models.json xp_first_level and ship_level_growth. skills: the bonus per skill level (speed: top speed +2%; durability: wear and breakdown chance -5%; efficiency: fuel burn -3%; range, tugs only in place of durability: reach +15%), up to skill_max_level each. skill_costs: each skill level also costs money, first x the model's price for a skill's 1st level plus step more for each level it already has (5%, 7.5% ... 27.5% for the 10th), each skill priced separately.
_mega_comment: Mega upgrade: once a model has max_owned ships, all at ship_max_level, it can be bought once for cost_factor x the model's price (Scooter 20: $1,000,000). Every ship of that model then gets speed_bonus more top speed and profit_bonus more profit on each profitable trade (recovery boats: speed_bonus more top speed and recovery_fuel_saving less fuel burn). recovery_xp: a recovery boat earns per_nm XP for every mile of a finished recovery job (out to the lost ship and carrying it to port), and the company earns company_share of the XP the rescued ship's full hold would earn over the miles it was carried. Not for recovery boats.
_tugs_comment: Tugs (ship_models.json tug): you can own per_port of them for each port on your ships' routes, each based at the route port with the fewest (the busiest first). A ship lost within a tug's reach (reach_nm, more with the range skill) of either end of its leg is fetched by the free tugs based at the nearer end that can reach it (up to per_port), before any recovery boat: they sail out, turn round and push or drag it back to their port at tow_factor x each one's speed, added up (so two tow it twice as fast as one). Each earns recovery_xp per_nm for every mile of the job.
_port_sizes_comment: Port sizes run 1 to max: bands are [name, smallest size] (Small 1-25, Medium 26-50, Large 51-75, Giant 76-100); ports.json size is where each starts. A port grows by the cargo value the player's ships load and unload there: value / (growth_value_per_point x its size) points (bigger ports need more), banked up to max_pending and applied at up to max_growth_per_hour. Tuned so a mid-game company's busiest port (about $60M an hour through a size-50 port) climbs a band in about 15 hours, and no port faster than a band in 5 hours. From company level shrink_from_level, a port above shrink_floor loses shrink_per_hour (a band in about 30 hours), less whatever it grows, never going below shrink_floor. Sizes in the normal range play as before sizes; toward size 1 the player's trades move prices up to impact_at_min times as much (and their effect lasts that much longer) and fuel and repairs cost costs_at_min more, and toward max impact_at_max and costs_at_max. ship_models.json min_port is the smallest band a model can dock at.
_hubs_comment: Headquarters and hubs: the HQ is at the home port from the start; one more hub every every_company_levels company levels, up to max_hubs, each placed for good at any port. A hub earns the XP of every delivery unloaded at its port and levels 0 to max_level; level L to L+1 costs (level_minutes[0] + level_minutes[1] x L) minutes of traffic_share of a full fleet's XP at the current company level, so a hub taking about a quarter of the fleet's deliveries maxes out in about 6 hours. Each level is an upgrade point for 4 paths of up to max_path_level points, and spending one costs upgrade_cost plus upgrade_cost_step for each point already in that path (2M, 2.5M, 3M...); per_point is each point's bonus to every ship docking there (xp: ship XP, costs: fuel and repair prices, speed: port stop time, pay: the price cargo sells for there). Every delivery unloaded at a hub also earns the company more XP: company_xp_base plus company_xp_per_10_levels for every 10 hub levels (+10% at level 0, +50% at level 40). The HQ's bonuses, this one included, are hq_multiplier times a hub's. industry: each hub (and the HQ) has a plot for an industry beside its marina, room for one more building as it reaches each of slot_levels; each building is one commodity's (one of each per hub), costs price, and demolishing it refunds refund of that. For its commodity at its port it makes the buy price buy_discount cheaper, the sell price sell_bonus more expensive, and deliveries (unloaded there, or loaded there) earn xp_bonus more XP, the HQ's hq_multiplier times as much.
_regions_comment: Market regions (markets.json regions) start locked, all but the home port's: shaded on the map, their ports nameless and unclickable, and no route or hub can use them (ships may sail through). One more region can be unlocked every every_company_levels company levels, chosen on the World map (all 17 by level 80).
_company_types_comment: Company types: a new company starts as one type (chosen on the New Company screen) and its lines' tiers unlock at company level start + tier_levels[tier - 1] (1, 4, 9, 16, 25 for the starting type, counted from level 1). Every pick_every company levels (15, 30, 45, 60) it picks one more type it doesn't have yet (GameState.choose_company_type()), whose tiers unlock the same way counted from that level. Ship categories not in any type (recovery boats, tugs, icebreakers) keep their ship_models.json unlock_level for everyone, as does every model for a company from before types (every type open, shown as All). categories: the ship_models.json categories each type sells; tab: its Shop tab; color: its icon's color (CompanyTypeIcon draws the icon by id). coming_soon: a type not playable yet (Cruises, until its voyages are built): it can't be chosen, and its models (ship_models.json coming_soon) are only shown in the Shop's coming-soon tab.

types.name: Cargo & Ore
types.blurb: Container ships with toys, clothing, furniture and coffee, and bulk carriers with iron ore, coal and gold.

types.name: Vehicles
types.blurb: Car carriers rolling cars, trucks and boats from the factories to the showrooms, from a river barge to a giant ro-ro.

types.name: Agriculture
types.blurb: Grain carriers with wheat, corn, soybeans, rice and barley, and livestock carriers with cattle, sheep and pigs.

types.name: Tankers
types.blurb: Oil and gas, from a bunker tanker topping up ships in harbour to a supertanker crossing oceans.

types.name: Seafood
types.blurb: Fishing and crabbing boats working the grounds for salmon, tuna and king crab, and reefers carrying the catch to market.

types.name: Cruises
types.blurb: Cruise lines: Ocean cruisers filling big ships at big ports, and Expedition cruisers taking a few guests to the ice, the wildlife and the wonders. You set the itineraries, the cabins, the prices and the service.
